title: Hearty Crumbly Earthly Polish Bake
description: A warm, comforting dish perfect for post-workout nourishment, featuring the earthy flavors of ground nut oil and double-rise bread, all in a traditional Polish-style earthy crust.
instructions: In a large bowl, crumble the double-rise bread into small pieces.
In a separate bowl, mix together the ground nut oil, caraway seeds, onion, garlic, potato starch, and apple cider vinegar until well combined.
Add the dry ingredients to the bread pieces and stir until a sticky dough forms.
Gradually add the warm water to the dough, mixing until a smooth, pliable dough forms.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for 5-7 minutes, until it becomes elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.
Prep a 9-inch (23cm) round baking dish or kazán-cauldron with parchment paper and a small amount of cooking oil.
Punch down the dough and transfer it to the prepared baking dish.
Dust the top of the dough with oats for a crunchy topping.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 190°F (88°C).
Remove from the oven and let cool for 10-15 minutes before slicing and serving.
Serve warm, garnished with chopped fresh herbs if desired.
Store leftovers in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.
Reheat in the oven at 350°F (180°C) for 5-10 minutes, or until warmed through.
Serve as a comforting dessert or snack after a workout, perfect for replenishing energy and satisfying hunger.
